Definition: from ἵκω (ἱκάνω or ἱκνέομαι, akin to G2240) (to arrive); competent (as if coming in season), i.e. ample (in amount) or fit (in character):--able, + content, enough, good, great, large, long (while), many, meet, much, security, sore, sufficient, worthy.
BiblicalUsage: hikanós means able, sufficient, worthy. It occurs 40 times in all, and the passages I have picked — Matthew, Mark, Luke, and Acts — show it in its plain sense. I read it as a word that does its work quietly, without dressing anything up.
TheologicalSignificance: What hikanós tells me is that God’s grace is sufficient, and His sufficiency is our sufficiency. I hold that reading it plainly keeps me honest about what God actually said.
